subject.declared_domain: The BM25 duplicate / dead-twin scanner (comp-dups). Scores a resource's NAME and file BODY -- what it IS -- as distinct from comp-similar, which scores a synthesized summary of what it DOES. Advisory and read-only by its own declaration: emits a ranked candidate ledger plus a suppression audit, and never removes.

methodology.how: Three tiers over a corpus of tokenized 'documents'. A vendored BM25 class (:84) with k1=1.5 and b=0.75 scores neighbors; suppressors remove DESIGNED parallels before anything is reported (cross-firm same-name, environment triplets, per-agent-tree paths, service suffixes); a dead-prior regex raises candidates under deprecated/archive-shaped paths, and by CTO arch-gate condition 2 a finding is 'CONFIRMED dead' ONLY after a graph reachability check shows zero consumers -- otherwise it is 'INFERRED dead, graph-pending'. THE BURIED OPINIONS, IN PROSE because the TO's form is prose: (1) max_df_ratio=0.25 at :98 -- a token appearing in more than 25% of documents is SKIPPED ENTIRELY for candidate generation, so the operative definition of 'similar' silently excludes the estate's most common vocabulary; (2) df_cut has a floor of 2, so on a tiny corpus almost nothing is excluded and the ratio stops meaning what it says; (3) top=5 and min_score=0.0 defaults, so a sixth genuine twin is invisible and a score of exactly 0.0 is dropped; (4) _FIRMS is 12 HARDCODED firm names and _SERVICE_SUFFIX 13 hardcoded suffixes -- a new firm or suffix is silently un-suppressed; (5) _DEAD_PRIOR_RE hardcodes 7 directory names as evidence of death; (6) _DDB_WINDOW_DAYS=30, and that one carries its own written rationale, which the others do not; (7) _HELD_PREFIXES exempts 2 hardcoded paths. EVERY ONE IS A DEFINITIONAL CHOICE ABOUT WHAT COUNTS AS A DUPLICATE, and none is reachable without reading the source.
declared_opinions: max_df_ratio=0.25 at :98 -- a token appearing in more than 25% of documents is SKIPPED ENTIRELY for candidate generation, so the operative definition of 'similar' silently excludes the estate's most common vocabulary.
df_cut carries a floor of max(N*ratio, 2), so on a small corpus almost nothing is excluded and the ratio stops meaning what it says.
BM25 k1=1.5 and b=0.75 -- standard defaults, with no record of tuning against this corpus.
neighbors() defaults top=5 and min_score=0.0, so a sixth genuine twin is invisible and a zero score is dropped rather than reported.
_FIRMS is 12 HARDCODED firm names and _SERVICE_SUFFIX 13 hardcoded suffixes; a firm or suffix outside those lists is NOT suppressed, so its designed parallels surface as duplicate candidates.
_DEAD_PRIOR_RE hardcodes 7 directory names (deprecated/archive/archived/old/legacy/_attic/graveyard) as evidence of death; a dead file outside those paths raises no prior.
_DDB_WINDOW_DAYS=30 -- and this one carries a written rationale in-line, which the other cutoffs do not.

coverage.universe: repo files eligible to be scored as duplicate candidates, after the suppressors and the discriminative-token cut have removed designed parallels and common vocabulary
coverage.denominator_absent_reason: THE POPULATION IS NOT A FIXED SET AND IS DEFINED PER INVOCATION. The scanned corpus is assembled at call time from the caller's path arguments, then reduced by four suppressor families, a vendor-dir exclusion, a held-prefix exemption and the max_df_ratio=0.25 token cut -- so 'N of M' has no stable M without fixing an invocation. ⛔ I DID NOT RUN A FULL SCAN TO PRODUCE ONE, and inventing a repo-file count here would be a denominator for a population the tool does not actually score. Stating the reason is the lawful form (v2 makes a bare null rejectable); a fabricated M would pass the field and mislead the consumer.
explicitly_out: tokens present in >25% of documents -- excluded from candidate generation entirely by max_df_ratio, so the most common estate vocabulary cannot contribute a match
cross-firm same-name pairs, environment triplets, per-agent-tree paths and service-suffix variants -- suppressed as DESIGNED parallels, with the suppression logged rather than silent
vendored directories (_VENDOR_DIRS) and 2 hardcoded held prefixes (_HELD_PREFIXES)
any firm not among the 12 hardcoded in _FIRMS, and any service suffix not among the 13 -- these are NOT suppressed, so they can surface as false duplicates

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: EXERCISED: invoked with a nonexistent path argument the module exits rc=2 and prints its own usage/error rather than an empty ledger; invoked with --help it exits rc=0 with the scanner description. A path that exists but contains no scoreable files returns an EMPTY RANKED LEDGER with rc=0 -- which is the ambiguous case.
silent_degrade_paths: ⛔ AN EMPTY CANDIDATE LEDGER HAS THREE INDISTINGUISHABLE CAUSES: (a) genuinely no duplicates, (b) every candidate suppressed as a designed parallel, (c) the query's tokens all exceeded max_df_ratio and were skipped, so no candidates were ever generated. The suppression audit distinguishes (b) -- it is printed and logged -- but nothing distinguishes (c) from (a).
A firm absent from the 12-entry _FIRMS list is not suppressed, so its designed cross-firm parallels surface as duplicate CANDIDATES -- a false positive that reads exactly like a real finding.
The dead-prior regex keys on 7 directory NAMES, so a genuinely dead file outside those paths raises no prior at all.
failure_mode.evidence: EXERCISED per COX2-AC7, with rc read WITHOUT a pipeline (a piped `| tail` returns tail's rc, which caught me three times across these two waves): nonexistent-path invocation -> rc=2 with an error; --help -> rc=0. distinguishable='no' is the MEASURED verdict for the empty-ledger case and it is the high-value finding on this subject: the tool is honest about suppression (it logs what it hid, by explicit arch-gate condition) but has no signal at all for the max_df_ratio path, so a scan that generated zero candidates and a scan that found zero duplicates print the same thing. silent_degrade_paths is INFERRED -- reasoned from source, not each route exercised -- and marked rather than absorbed into 'measured'.

verdict.why: Every row is worked, the defects are named with owners, and the tool is usable within stated limits. WHAT HOLDS: a real, correctly-formed BM25 (settling a wave-1 claim of mine that was made without opening the file); four suppressor families that LOG what they hide rather than suppressing silently, which is a deliberate arch-gate condition and the opposite of the failure mode this project keeps finding; and a CONFIRMED-vs-INFERRED dead distinction that refuses to call a file dead on a path name alone. WHAT QUALIFIES IT: (1) an empty candidate ledger cannot be distinguished from a scan whose tokens were all cut by max_df_ratio -- distinguishable_from_true_negative='no', the single most valuable thing this card surfaces; (2) seven definitional choices about what COUNTS as a duplicate are reachable only by reading the source, and one of them (a 25% document-frequency cut) silently removes the estate's most common vocabulary from consideration; (3) the population is invocation-scoped, so no stable coverage denominator exists and the row is honestly 'absent'; (4) 12 hardcoded firms and 13 hardcoded suffixes mean a new firm produces false positives rather than a gap. NOT UNSOUND: nothing here blocks load-bearing use of a tool that declares itself advisory, never removes, and requires graph corroboration before any death claim. || SEMANTIC-AXIS DECLARATION: NOT SYSTEMATICALLY EXAMINED. The seven opinions came into view because the coverage and failure_mode rows forced them, not from a deliberate sweep. I did NOT audit whether k1=1.5/b=0.75 were ever tuned for this corpus, whether 0.25 reflects a ruled intent or a v1 guess, or whether the 12 firms still match the estate. Every instrument I used -- source reads, greps, rc checks -- is structurally blind to a deprecated opinion. || GENERATOR CURRENCY: materializer_standing='not_applicable'; this module materializes no layer, a MEASURED absence of applicability rather than an unmeasured currency.
